mappings.Perelman defined λ as the infimum of F o: Perelman defined λ as the infimum of F over normalized f, showing it is nondecreasing along the flow. For expanding breathers, he used the scale-invariant $\bar{\lambda} = \lambda V^{2/n}$ and proved strict monotonicity unless on a gradient soliton. For shrinking breathers, he introduced the $W$-functional with a scale parameter $\tau$ and proved monotonicity via formula (3.4), ruling out nontrivial shrinking breathers. This established that Ricci flow on closed manifolds has no periodic orbits in the space of metrics modulo diffeomorphism and scaling.
mappings.The paper defines h and shows it belongs: The paper defines h and shows it belongs to $M_{-2}^{!}(\Gamma_0(2))$. The functions psi_I, psi_T, psi_S are defined as combinations of h and its images under the slash operator. The identity psi_T + psi_S = psi_I is proven using group relations. These functions have Fourier expansions (49)–(51) used for asymptotic estimates. The construction is essential for defining b(x).
